Specimen: Lung biopsy
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL HISTORY
Elderly female with lung adenocarcinoma. ROS1 immunohistochemistry showed 2+ staining.

TEST PERFORMED
ROS1 Gene Rearrangement Analysis by Fluorescence In Situ Hybridization (FISH)

METHODOLOGY
Interphase FISH analysis was performed on formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded lung biopsy tissue using the Vysis LSI ROS1 (6q22) Dual Color Break Apart Rearrangement Probe (Abbott Molecular). This probe consists of a 5' ROS1 probe labeled in SpectrumGreen and a 3' ROS1 probe labeled in SpectrumOrange.

RESULTS
ROS1 (6q22) FISH: NEGATIVE for ROS1 rearrangement

Cells analyzed: 50
Normal pattern (2 fusion signals): 47 cells (94%)
Gain pattern (3-4 fusion signals): 3 cells (6%)
Rearranged pattern: 0 cells (0%)

Positive threshold: ≥15% of cells with split signals

INTERPRETATION
No ROS1 gene rearrangement was detected. The presence of 2-3 copies of intact ROS1 in a small subset of cells is of unclear clinical significance and may represent chromosomal polysomy or focal amplification. The positive ROS1 immunohistochemistry in the absence of ROS1 rearrangement may be due to protein overexpression through alternative mechanisms.

CLINICAL IMPLICATIONS
This patient is unlikely to benefit from ROS1-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., crizotinib, entrectinib) due to the absence of ROS1 rearrangement. Alternative molecular targets should be considered for therapeutic decision-making.

Pathologist: [redacted name], MD
Board Certified in Molecular Genetic Pathology
